summary: Jefferson County 100-foot Aermotor steel tower erected March 1956; dismantled around 2003, with its top 80 feet re-erected at a Madison County hunting preserve.

facts.status_note: Dismantled around 2003. The top 80 feet were re-erected at the Gum Creek Hunting Preserve in Madison County. No source confirms that the structure still stands there.

access.note: The record describes the re-erected top section as a private observation tower and names no public access.

events.note: A 100-foot Aermotor steel tower was erected
Dismantled into sections, date given as c.2003; top 80 feet re-erected at the Gum Creek Hunting Preserve, Madison County

evidence.quote: A 100-foot Aermotor steel tower was erected.
The tower was dismantled into sections.

evidence.supports: Dismantling date marked as approximate, c.2003
Top 80 feet re-erected as a private observation tower at Gum Creek Hunting Preserve, Madison County
evidence.quote: The top 80-feet was erected as a private observation tower at the Gum Creek Hunting Preserve in Madison County.

evidence.supports: Company also manufactured galvanized steel fire lookout towers (general, not specific to Ashville)
evidence.quote: The company also manufactured galvanized steel fire lookout towers

corrections.why: The source says the tower was dismantled around 2003 and its top 80 feet re-erected elsewhere, so it is not simply gone.
The source names no agency. T2N R6E is a township and range survey location, not an agency.

notes_for_editor: Single source (Eastern U.S. Lookouts). Two WebSearch queries, plus reads of the RadioReference Jefferson and Madison County pages, found no tower and no record of the Gum Creek Hunting Preserve. A search surfaced a Greenville Advocate article titled 'Fire tower taken down, moved, set to be restored' that may or may not concern this tower. The site returns HTTP 403 to both fetch_text and WebFetch, so the article is unread. The source does not say what became of the lower 20 feet, so the story leaves that out. The brief's design and 30.5 m height match the 100-foot Aermotor line. Coordinates are unchecked. The Aermotor sentence in the story draws on Wikipedia's general note that the company manufactured galvanized steel fire lookout towers. Nothing ties that model to Ashville, so the story does not claim it.
